# Add pressed background, text, and glyph tokens to Neo.button.Base

Please comment to claim before starting; check current assignees and linked PRs.

## Context

Surfaced during review of `neomjs/neo-pro#146` (`neomjs/neo-pro#145`, `PRR_kwDOVg8fac8AAAABXGZm0g`), where grouping preset and summary toolbar buttons set `pressed: true` (`Neo.button.Base#afterSetPressed` toggling `.pressed` on the button root).

- **Design authority:** `src/button/Base.mjs:59-64` and `src/button/Base.mjs:379-388` (`pressed_` config: *"pressed state for buttons; toggles the `'pressed'` class on the button element via `NeoArray.toggle(cls, 'pressed', value === true)`"*) together with `#18141` / `#18171` (every `&.pressed` button variant in `resources/scss/src/` must read flat theme tokens declared across all 5 theme sheets, and `theme-neo-dark` / `theme-neo-light` must give pressed buttons a visually distinct state).

## The Problem

`Neo.button.Base` provides first-class `pressed_` state (`src/button/Base.mjs:59-64`, `:379-388`), and `resources/scss/src/button/Base.scss` styles `&.pressed` across all four button UIs (`primary`/default, `--secondary`, `--ghost`, `--tertiary`). However:

1. **Structural stylesheet only consumes border tokens on `&.pressed`:**
   - `resources/scss/src/button/Base.scss:332-334` (`&.pressed { border: var(--button-border-pressed); }`)
   - `resources/scss/src/button/Base.scss:96-98` (`.neo-button-secondary.pressed { border: var(--button-secondary-border-pressed); }`)
   - `resources/scss/src/button/Base.scss:176-178` (`.neo-button-ghost.pressed { border: var(--button-ghost-border-pressed); }`)
   - `resources/scss/src/button/Base.scss:253-255` (`.neo-button-tertiary.pressed { border: var(--button-tertiary-border-pressed); }`)
   None of the four `&.pressed` blocks consume pressed background, text, or glyph color tokens (`--button-*-background-color-pressed`, `--button-*-text-color-pressed`, `--button-*-glyph-color-pressed`).
2. **Stock `theme-neo-dark` and `theme-neo-light` set `--button-*-border-pressed` identical to unpressed:**
   - In both `resources/scss/theme-neo-dark/button/Base.scss` and `resources/scss/theme-neo-light/button/Base.scss`:
     - `--button-border-pressed: none` (identical to `--button-border: none` at line 23)
     - `--button-secondary-border-pressed: var(--cmp-button-borderwidth) solid var(--cmp-button-secondary-border-default)` (identical to `--button-secondary-border` at line 55)
     - `--button-ghost-border-pressed: none` (identical to `--button-ghost-border: none` at line 85)
     - `--button-tertiary-border-pressed: none` (identical to `--button-tertiary-border: none` at line 117)
   As a result, setting `pressed: true` on a stock `Neo.button.Base` in `neo-theme-neo-dark` or `neo-theme-neo-light` produces zero computed-style difference from `pressed: false`, forcing consumers (such as `neomjs/neo-pro`'s `progridgrouping` toolbar in `neomjs/neo-pro#146`) to write an app-local `.neo-button.pressed` override block.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/button/Base.mjs:379-388` — `afterSetPressed(value, oldValue)` toggles `'pressed'` on `this.cls`.
- `resources/scss/src/button/Base.scss`:
  - Primary/default `&.pressed` (`:332-334`)
  - `.neo-button-secondary` `&.pressed` (`:96-98`)
  - `.neo-button-ghost` `&.pressed` (`:176-178`)
  - `.neo-button-tertiary` `&.pressed` (`:253-255`)
- All 5 theme sheets carrying `button/Base.scss` (`#18141` nested-theme reset rule):
  - `resources/scss/theme-neo-dark/button/Base.scss`
  - `resources/scss/theme-neo-light/button/Base.scss`
  - `resources/scss/theme-dark/button/Base.scss`
  - `resources/scss/theme-light/button/Base.scss`
  - `resources/scss/theme-cyberpunk/button/Base.scss`
- Sibling precedent: `#18171` (`resources/scss/src/tab/header/Button.scss:67`, which reads `--tab-button-glyph-color-pressed` and `--tab-button-text-color-pressed` on `&.pressed` and declares them in every theme sheet carrying `tab/header/Button.scss`).

## The Fix

1. **Extend `resources/scss/src/button/Base.scss` `&.pressed` rules** across the four button variants (`default`, `secondary`, `ghost`, `tertiary`) to apply:
   - `background-color: var(--button-<variant>-background-color-pressed)` (and `--button-background-color-pressed` on base)
   - `border: var(--button-<variant>-border-pressed)`
   - `.neo-button-text { color: var(--button-<variant>-text-color-pressed); }`
   - `.neo-button-glyph { color: var(--button-<variant>-glyph-color-pressed); }`
2. **Declare the pressed token set in all 5 `resources/scss/theme-*/button/Base.scss` files** (`theme-neo-dark`, `theme-neo-light`, `theme-dark`, `theme-light`, `theme-cyberpunk`):
   - In `theme-neo-dark` and `theme-neo-light`, bind pressed background, border, text, and glyph tokens to visually distinct active/contrast semantic tokens (e.g. `--cmp-button-*-surface-active`, `--sem-color-border-focused` / `--cmp-button-secondary-border-hover`, `--sem-color-fg-neutral-contrast`) so a `pressed: true` button is visually distinguishable from `pressed: false` in both themes out of the box.
   - In `theme-dark`, `theme-light`, and `theme-cyberpunk`, declare each new `--button-*-background-color-pressed`, `--button-*-text-color-pressed`, and `--button-*-glyph-color-pressed` token so nested theme boundaries reset cleanly per `#18141`.
3. **Compile CSS outputs** via `npm run build-themes` (or targeted theme build) and verify with a Playwright component/unit spec asserting computed `backgroundColor`, `borderColor`, and text/glyph `color` differ between `pressed: false` and `pressed: true` in both `neo-theme-neo-dark` and `neo-theme-neo-light`.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--button-background-color-pressed`, `--button-text-color-pressed`, `--button-glyph-color-pressed`, `--button-border-pressed` | `resources/scss/src/button/Base.scss:332-334` + `resources/scss/theme-*/button/Base.scss` | Applied on `.neo-button.pressed` (`background-color`, `border`, `.neo-button-text color`, `.neo-button-glyph color`) with distinct defaults in `theme-neo-dark` and `theme-neo-light` | Declared in all 5 `theme-*/button/Base.scss` sheets per `#18141` | SCSS comments | Emitted CSS diff + Playwright computed-style spec |
| `--button-{secondary,ghost,tertiary}-{background-color,text-color,glyph-color,border}-pressed` | `resources/scss/src/button/Base.scss:96-98,176-178,253-255` + `resources/scss/theme-*/button/Base.scss` | Applied on `.neo-button-{secondary,ghost,tertiary}.pressed` with distinct defaults in `theme-neo-dark` and `theme-neo-light` | Declared in all 5 `theme-*/button/Base.scss` sheets per `#18141` | SCSS comments | Emitted CSS diff + Playwright computed-style spec |

## Decision Record impact

`none` — aligns with `#18141`, `#18145`, and `#18171` (flat component tokens in `resources/scss/theme-*/`, variant rules in `resources/scss/src/`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1:** `resources/scss/src/button/Base.scss` applies `--button-*-background-color-pressed`, `--button-*-border-pressed`, `--button-*-text-color-pressed`, and `--button-*-glyph-color-pressed` on `&.pressed` across default/primary, `secondary`, `ghost`, and `tertiary` button variants.
- [ ] **AC-2:** All 5 theme sheets with `button/Base.scss` (`theme-neo-dark`, `theme-neo-light`, `theme-dark`, `theme-light`, `theme-cyberpunk`) declare the new pressed tokens (`#18141` exact-name parity across themes).
- [ ] **AC-3:** In both `neo-theme-neo-dark` and `neo-theme-neo-light`, toggling `button.pressed = true` produces a computed `backgroundColor` and/or `borderColor` + label/glyph `color` distinct from `pressed: false`, verified by a Playwright test.
- [ ] **AC-4:** Built CSS themes (`dist/development/css/theme-*/button/Base.css` or equivalent) are regenerated cleanly and unit/component suites pass.

## Out of Scope

- `Neo.tab.header.Button` pressed tokens (already delivered in `#18171` / PR `#18212`).
- Retiring the temporary `.neo-button.pressed` token-repointing block in `neomjs/neo-pro`'s `resources/scss/src/apps/progridgrouping/Viewport.scss` (tracked in `neomjs/neo-pro` once this Engine leaf lands).

## Avoided Traps

- **Adding descendant `.pressed` selectors inside theme files:** per `#18145` and `#18171`, `pressed` is a class on `.neo-button` itself (`&.pressed`), and selector blocks belong in `resources/scss/src/button/Base.scss` while `resources/scss/theme-*/button/Base.scss` declare CSS custom properties only.
- **Declaring new tokens in `theme-neo-*` only:** per `#18141`, omitting new tokens from `theme-dark`, `theme-light`, or `theme-cyberpunk` leaks outer theme values across nested theme boundaries.

## Related

- `#18171` (PR `#18212` — `Neo.tab.header.Button` `&.pressed` glyph/text contrast tokens)
- `#18141` (cross-theme token declaration parity)
- `#18145` (theme files declare variables only; selectors live in `resources/scss/src/`)
- `#17241` (engine vs. app-layer visual affordance ownership)

### @neo-fable-clio - 2026-11-13T18:02:58Z

**A Look input from today's design read** (engine `c19cd4934a`, frames in `neo-theme-neo-dark` and `neo-theme-neo-light`).

Measured again today: with `ui` unset, `secondary`, `ghost` and `tertiary`, a button with the `pressed` class computes exactly like one without it in both neo themes. Two more example headers wait on this ticket: the zoom and option toggles of the scheduler and Gantt examples under #20874. They can set `ui: 'secondary'` and `pressed` today and show no state until this lands.

**A look for the default that has already been read in both themes**, on a consumer's toolbar of compact bordered buttons: pressed is the unpressed surface mixed with the primary surface, a 1 px border in the primary colour, and the contrast text colour at weight 600. Measured in neo-dark, pressed against unpressed:

| | pressed | unpressed |
|---|---|---|
| background | `color(srgb 0.10 0.14 0.28)` | `color(srgb 0.06 0.08 0.13)` |
| border | `1px rgb(62, 99, 221)` | `1px color(srgb 0.15 0.21 0.38)` |
| text | `rgb(255, 255, 255)`, 600 | `rgb(240, 241, 244)`, 500 |

For `ghost` and `tertiary`, which have no border at rest, the tinted background alone should carry the state.

**A criterion I propose** (the author's call): frames of the four variants, pressed beside unpressed, in both neo themes, read before merge. I hold that read for the families under #20874 and take it here too.

**Timing.** The claim of 2026-11-11 03:10Z runs until 2026-11-14 03:10Z under the three-day rule in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. The families under #20874 are due on `dev` by Thu 2026-11-19, so if the ticket is free on Sat 2026-11-14, I take it.

I'm taking this one for the Engine 14 cut, as a maintainer.

@Vijay431, thank you for claiming it. The claim lapsed on 14 Nov under the 3-day rule in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and no pull request followed. If you'd like another issue, the open [`good first issue`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/labels/good%20first%20issue) list has some, and a new one is filed every day of the release window.

**Why now.** The examples section is read on Fri 20 Nov, and three engine surfaces there show no pressed state. Measured on `dev` at `a56015e45b` in `neo-theme-neo-light`: the calendar's view switch renders Day, Week, Month and Year with the same `rgb(62, 99, 221)` background, no border and white text, and Week alone carries `aria-pressed="true"`. Five stylesheets have already written their own `.pressed` block because of this: `examples/gantt/basic`, `examples/scheduler/basic`, `examples/scheduler/bigData`, `examples/dashboard/desk` and `desktop/Taskbar`.

**Paths.** Since #21217 the sources are plain CSS: `resources/css/src/button/Base.css` and `resources/css/theme-*/button/Base.css`. They are the same files the body calls `resources/scss/…`.

**The look.** @neo-fable-clio's measured proposal above is my starting point: a tinted surface, a 1 px border in the primary colour and the contrast text at weight 600; for `ghost` and `tertiary` the tint alone. Her criterion is also adopted: the PR will show the four variants, pressed beside unpressed, in both neo themes, read before merge.

I'm removing `good first issue` and `help wanted` now that the ticket is owned and on the cut's path.
